translations.text: I, Samuel, by Christ Catholicos of Kartli, greet you with prayer in the Lord, lord John son of Saban, spiritual son of the holy catholic Church and our beloved!
Peace be upon you and upon all the household of your house through Christ!
We ourselves know your zeal for the service of God, your God-given knowledge of the divine books, and your diligence in striving after good works.
You yourself know about this blessed new martyr Abo, who in these our days was martyred, and is an intercessor with Christ for us and for all this land of ours, Kartli.
It is my wish that the martyrdom of this blessed man also be written down, like those of the earlier martyrs of Christ,
and that it too be placed in the holy catholic Church as a memorial for all who will come after us.
For this reason I have sent you this letter of mine by the hand of my priest Khsartan.
Now receive this letter of mine, my prayer, and the sign of the cross made by my hand, and with the help of God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit,
through the intercession of the holy Mother of God and of the holy apostles and martyrs, set to work recounting fully and truthfully
how it happened, as you yourself know it. Write down the martyrdom of the holy martyr Abo and send what you have written to us, so that we may pray all the more for you.
The grace of the Lord be upon you, Amen! From John.
I received the ever-desired and venerable command of my God-honored master and lord by the hand of the priest Khsartan, a lover of holiness.
For this I, unworthy as I am, raised my hands and gave thanks to the almighty and beneficent Christ our God,
who did not let my lowliness be forgotten in your holy prayers, which God accepts and which I have been made worthy to receive.
And all the more I praise and bless the mercy of God, who put it into my master's heart to give such a command,
which will become for me profit and fruit for the soul, and a boast and joy for the body, both for eternity and in this world as well.
Now what shall I say to your lordship? It is hard for me either way. If I disobey your command, it is written:
"A disobedient son shall be given over to destruction." And if I hasten to be obedient, it says about that too:
"Do not search into what is below you, and do not examine what is mightier than you."
Because of this, fear and anxiety seized me. My mind was troubled, I lost heart, and I fell short in understanding.
But I judged it better to make myself obedient to the command of my lord.

Through this I was strengthened again and raised up by your holy prayers, which are pleasing to God, and by the sign of the cross made over me, unworthy as I am, by your right hand, which always holds up offerings to God.
I also learned from the saying of Solomon, chief of the wise: "Imitate the ant, you sluggard, and become a worker like it."
Just as the ant diligently grapples with a grain of wheat larger than itself until it lifts it and carries it off as its food,
so I too set about diligently lifting what is beyond my strength. The Lord fulfilled the desire of my heart, and I wrote down the martyrdom as gathered by my unworthy mind,
…the true and unerring [account] of the holy martyr, by the grace and intercession of the blessed Abo, and I have sent it to you, my lord, for whose sake I again ask with supplication:
may the Lord make it pleasing to your heart and to the heart of all the Christ-loving faithful people who read it,
so that my unworthiness may again, now and hereafter, become a sharer in your prayers.
First chapter: An account and instruction for the assembly of the servants of God and lovers of the martyrs, and the commemoration of this new martyr Abo.
Second chapter: The coming of the blessed Abo into Kartli and his baptism.
Third chapter: The martyrdom of the holy Abo.
Fourth chapter: The praise of the blessed holy Abo.
Beloved of the Father, friends and servants of Christ the Son of God, and dwelling-places of the Holy Spirit!
I see you as those known by God and who know God; therefore I have called you servants and friends of Christ.
Servants, because "you were bought with his precious blood"; and friends, because we are his creation and his creatures, and through his love we have received baptism.

Now I beseech you in Christ: with eager hearts lend me those outward organs of hearing of yours, and still more open wide the perceiving ears of your heart and mind to listen, and become hosts to these words of mine,
for they are for the sake of Christ and of these blessed martyrs. Receive them into the tent of your body and prepare a dwelling for them,
for the Lord wishes to dwell within your members, as the holy apostle Paul, the teacher of the churches, said:
"You are temples of God, and the Holy Spirit dwells among you"; and the Lord says through the prophet:
"I will come and dwell among you"; and in the holy Gospel he says: "The kingdom of God is within your hearts."
Therefore, beloved, do not grow weary of hearing these words, so that we may not labour in vain:
I by speaking and you by listening, so that the Lord may give us together the reward of our labours.
And it is not for me alone to seek to hear this longed-for martyrdom of this holy martyr; rather, it is fitting for all of you also to marvel with me,
we who stand in this closing time, in the seventh age, about which time the Lord says:
"Many have gone astray, and they have led many astray." And the apostle Paul writes to Timothy:
"The time is coming when they will not endure the teaching of this life. Instead, following their own desires, they will gather teaching for themselves on their own authority
because their ears itch. They will turn their hearing away from the truth and turn to fables." This is now being fulfilled among us at this time.
For we who live in this corner of the earth suffer from the cruelty and malice of these overlords of ours, the rulers of this time, and from their deceitful devices.
Through the guile of their teaching and the laws they made up for themselves, these apostates from Christ have led many astray and turned them aside from the way of righteousness.
and have sinned against the truth of the Gospel of Christ, those who for five hundred years and even longer had been established in the faith by the holy grace of baptism.
From that time until now they have led astray those born of Christians: some by force, some by deceit, some through ignorance in their youth, some by cunning.
And the rest of us, who are believers, are enslaved under oppression and bound by want and poverty as if by iron,
beaten and tormented under their tribute and cruelly extorted. They waste away with fear and are shaken like reeds in strong winds.
But through love and fear of Christ, they keep to the ancestral way of life and endure their afflictions with patience, and so they do not turn away from the only-begotten Son of God.
At such a time this holy martyr appeared, valiant;
he was not one of us from the beginning. He did not know our faith; he was a stranger, of a foreign religion, and he came and to Christ our God
came to know him. Because of this, today this new feast and gathering in honor of the holy and new martyr has once again crowned the church,
and has lit up the whole Christian congregation together. On this day all people have been made worthy to offer overflowing thanks to Christ, our true God.
For this feast of the Theophany has become a double feast. The grace of God the Father, through revealing to us his beloved Son
and through the descent of his Holy Spirit, has placed on the head of the church the crown of his martyrs, woven by faith,
and from it the multitude of feasts surrounds the church like a crown. Those who love God have the custom of always gathering in the church for the glory of God.
For by gathering together they show much devotion to God. No insatiable appetite for vain luxuries and gluttonous eating is found among them;
instead of all tasty foods, the power of divine words comes sweetly from their mouths, for the words of the prophet resound among them:
"How sweet are your words to my palate, O Lord, sweeter than honey to my mouth." For a gathering to eat comes to the point of being full,
but souls who love God are never full when they recall the words of God.
And again: "Who that loves the martyrs could ever have enough of commemorating the holy martyrs?"
Such a gathering also shows wholehearted devotion to the Lord, for the Lord says to his saints: "Whoever has received you has received me."
For this reason their gathering for divine things is all the more eager. There, in their midst, the words of life are brought forward;
there faith in the Holy Trinity flourishes; there are the sweet teachings, the instructions of grace, the beauty of the patriarchs,
the glories of the prophets, the preaching of the apostles, the struggles of the martyrs, Christ taking our debt upon himself, and his suffering for us.
For the young, the story of the courage of Christ's struggle becomes strength and joy. For the old, remembering the martyrs' contest becomes a source of pride and gladness.
For the priests and the children, the disciples and sons of the church, the gathering for the feast of the saints is something they desire and long for, and
in the church their voices become like the voices of the angels who sing hymns, and the Holy Spirit, who is worshipped, rejoices among them,
and so that the Father may be glorified, and the love for humankind and the kindness of the Son may be proclaimed.
For the almighty God and most generous Lord did not ignore the grief of humankind. Out of love for humankind he put on flesh from the holy Virgin,
and by that holy flesh of his he raised up to heaven the fallen man who had been driven out of Paradise, and made him worthy of that incomprehensible mystery,
what he was not; and he remained what he was. This is the glory of our Saviour Jesus Christ in his humbling of himself for our sake.
For he humbled himself and saved us. He rose up to heaven, from where he had come down, took up with him this humanity that is from the earth, and is seated at the right hand of the Father.
The Godhead united this humanity to itself by a wondrous dispensation. By both these names he is one Son, God and man without division,
and the same one is proclaimed "by the name Emmanuel, God with us," and man, so that at his name every knee should bow,
of those in heaven, on earth and in the underworld, and "every tongue should confess" his name.
For his name is awesome and holy, all-powerful and wonderful; it is Lord and Almighty.
We cannot reach the riches of him. But as far as my weakness allows, and in answer to your eagerness, I will begin to tell you,
beloved, about these names: door, way, lamb, shepherd, stone, pearl, flower, angel, man, God, light, earth, salt, worm,
grain of mustard, sun of righteousness, Son of the immortal Father, and one God, unchanging, undiminished and unalterable.
For that nature is unchanging and undiminished after the taking on of flesh and its union with the Godhead.
So if we are able to explain each of these names truly to you, it is only by his grace that I will explain them to you, lovers of Christ.
He was called "door," for he said, "I am the door of the sheep." Truly, we who believe in him enter through him, as through the door of the Kingdom.
He was called "way," for he said, "I am the way and the truth and the life." He becomes the way for us who ascend to heaven.
He was called "lamb," "for he was slain for us." Yet he is ever living, and by sharing out his flesh and blood to us he grants us eternal life.
He was called "shepherd," for he said, "I am the good shepherd."

Truly he brought us, the straying sheep, back. With the staff of the cross he killed the lion, our enemy. By the power of his Godhead he brought back to life the body of the first-created man, which had been set free from the lion. And the bite
of that venomous wolf he healed by his own wounds, and he drove out that deadly venom with the medicine of his Godhead. So he fulfilled the word spoken by the prophet:
"He was wounded for our sins, and by his wounds we were healed."
The prophet called him the "cornerstone," for he is the one
who was despised and rejected by the high priests and scribes of the Jewish nation in Jerusalem. Yet this stone became the head of all the ends of heaven.
He was called "pearl," for like a pearl between two shells, the soul and the body, he shines out with Godhead,
whom those God-loving merchants of the kingdom, not as God alone (bare God) nor as mere man, but as God and man,
seek with faith, and they buy that single pearl of great price by spending all their wealth and even by shedding their own blood.

He was called salt, because he drew near to this flesh of ours, corrupted by sin, and took away from us the stench of idol-worship, and seasoned our souls, making them fragrant with faith in the worship of God.

He was called a flower, because he sprang up as a flower from the root of Jesse for the church, in the flesh, from the holy Virgin Mary, and with the fragrance of his divinity he poured out the Spirit of grace upon us.
He was called an angel, because the prophet calls him "Angel of great counsel, Wonderful," who came from the Father as our savior.
He was called a man, because the prophet said: "He is a man, and who will know him?"
Truly he put on perfect humanity, without sin, and revealed his divinity to us.
He was called God, as the blessed John the Evangelist said: "The Word was God, and all things were made through him, whatever was made."
He was called light by the same evangelist, for he said: "There was the true light, which enlightens every man coming into the world."
He was called earth, as David said: "The earth has yielded its fruit; may you bless us, O God, our God!"
Truly the creator of the earth came to earth, and from those made of earth, out of dust, that flesh of earthly nature, like beautiful green grass,
sprang up from the earth and brought forth as its fruit his holy apostles, martyrs and righteous ones, and he filled that cursed earth with the fruit of blessing.
He was called a mustard seed, because he makes himself small and becomes like us in our stature,
so that he might be planted in the field of our soul and spread his roots deep, and gather us upon the branches of his cross, and be raised up and raise us up with him.
He was called a worm, because he said: "I am a worm and not a man." With the radiance of his divinity,
as a hook within a worm, so he hid his divinity within his own flesh, and cast it down into the depths of this world and drew it up again, like a good fisherman, concerning which it says:
"He caught the dragon with a hook, and put a halter on its jaw and a ring in its nose"; that is, the devil,
whom he caught, and he crushed his schemes, as the psalmist David testifies: "You crushed the heads of the dragon."
He was called the sun of righteousness, because the prophet said: "And for you who fear his name the sun of righteousness will shine forth,
which has healing under its wings"; for he is the one who shelters and warms, and there is nothing hidden from his heat.
Yet I have not explained these things to you on my own authority, beloved ones, lovers of Christ and strivers after learning,
but with testimonies from the prophetic books and according to the preaching of the apostles, the writings of the holy Gospels, and the faith defined by the blessed fathers and teachers.
For unwavering faith is a great treasure for believers, O heavenly Father, God and Lord, giver of life,
through the grace received from you, for the faith of Christians is a great teaching.
Through this grace the righteous bow down to you, the saints bless you, the martyrs confess you, and for your sake they are made worthy of persecution,
you who suffered for us, O Christ God. They are witnesses to you, they make supplication to you, and they hold in contempt the deceit of the devil and the tyranny of his servants.
For not only did the Greeks obtain this faith that comes from God, but we too, the inhabitants of these distant lands, as the Lord testifies when he says:
"They will come from the east and from the west and will recline in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob."

Behold, the inhabitants of Kartli too have the faith, and it is called the mother of saints, some of whom are natives of this place, and some foreigners who have come among us from elsewhere from time to time,
who have been revealed as martyrs through Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
For there was a time when the prince (erismtavari) of Kartli, named Nerse, son of Adrnerse, curopalates and prince,

was summoned to the land of Babylon by the ruler of the Saracens at that time, the Commander of the Faithful (Amir al-Mu'minin) Abdallah, who resided in the great city of Baghdad, which he himself had built.
And on the denunciation of evil men he threw Nerse, the duke (eristavi) of this land of Kartli, into prison,
and he was held captive there for a period of three years, until, by the command of God, Abdallah the Commander of the Faithful died, and his son Mahdi took the throne in his place.
Then the beneficent God persuaded the heart of Mahdi, the Commander of the Faithful, to release Nerse,
and he brought him out of that bitter prison and sent him back here, to his own land, once again holding the rule of prince.
Now, lovers of Christ, I wish from this point on to tell you about this holy and blessed martyr Abo: what he was and of what kind, and from where he came here.
He was born of the stock of Abraham, from the sons of Ishmael, of the tribe of the Saracens, and not of foreign seed, nor born of a concubine, but wholly of the seed of the Arabs
on both his father's and his mother's side. His father and his mother, his brothers and his sisters were all there in the city of Baghdad in Babylon.
He was a youth, a young man of about eighteen years, or somewhat less, seventeen [?].
He wished to come here with the prince Nerse, and he attached himself to him as a servant.
He was skilled, expert at compounding fragrant ointments, and he was learned in the letters of the Saracens, the sons of Ishmael, the sons of Abraham, the descendants of Hagar.
But his coming out from there to our country was not something he decided on by himself.
Rather, just as the Lord said to the blessed Abraham in that same land of the Chaldeans,
"Go out from your land and from your kindred and from your father's house, and come to the land that I will show you,"
so too this man, again a descendant of Abraham, was called, not by his own intention but at God's prompting, and he left father and mother, brothers and sisters, kinsfolk, possessions and estates,
and, just as the Lord says in the holy Gospel, he came here as a fellow traveller with Nerse for the love of Christ.
When he came to Kartli, he lived with Nerse the duke. By his virtue he became beloved of all the people, and he learned to read and write Georgian and to speak it fluently.
Then he began to study the holy, divine books of the Old and New Testaments closely, for the Lord gave him understanding.
He would come to the holy church and listen constantly to the holy Gospels and to the readings from the prophets and apostles.
He would question and learn from many who were learned in the faith. Some opposed him as if in dispute, but even they became a means of learning for him.
In this way he became complete in all the teaching that the holy catholic Church has from Christ.
Then he cast aside the law of Muhammad and abandoned the rite of prayer of his fathers. He came to love Christ with all his heart and chose him, saying these words:
"The lawless told me tales [about it], but it was not so; [it is] as your faith [teaches]."
But he could not openly declare himself fully a Christian. Instead he fasted and prayed to Christ in secret, and he looked for a safe place
where he might receive the baptism of Christ, for he was afraid of the Saracens, the masters of the world who rule over us.
In those days the Saracen rulers again grew angry with Nerse the duke, and he fled,
for the Saracen army was fighting fiercely against him. The Lord protected him from their hands, and he passed through the Gate of Ossetia, which is called Darial.
When he went out, about three hundred men of his people were with him. Among them was this blessed servant of Christ, Abo.
Nerse, a fugitive from his own land, entered the northern land, where the dwelling places and encampments of the sons of Magog are.
These are the Khazars: wild men, fearsome in appearance, beasts by nature, eaters of blood. They have no religion, but they know only God the Creator.
When Nerse the duke came to the king of the Khazars, the king received him because he was a stranger and a fugitive from his enemies. He gave food and clothing to him and to all his people.
Then the blessed Abo saw that he was out of reach of the fear and oppression of the Saracens.
So he hastened to draw near to Christ and was baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit by the hands of honourable priests.
By the grace of the Holy Spirit there are many cities and villages in that northern land that live by the faith of Christ without fear.
From then on the blessed Abo, filled all the more with the grace of Christ, gave himself to fasting and prayer without hindrance.
After some time, Nerse asked the northern king to let him go from there to the land of Abkhazia.
He had already sent ahead his mother, his wife, his children, his possessions and all his household, because that land was safe from fear of the Saracens.
God softened the heart of the northern king, and he let Nerse go with many gifts.
They set out with joy and with thanks to God. They passed through the land of the pagans, who do not know God at all, and travelled without fear day and night on a journey of three months.
And all those days on the journey the blessed Abo prayed and fasted, and he never ceased from singing psalms.
And when they reached the land of Abkhazia, the prince of that land received Nerse together with all his people. When Nerse saw the queen,
his mother, and his wife and his sons, they all blessed God with joy because they had been gathered together alive and in peace.
Then, when the prince of Abkhazia learned about the blessed Abo, that he was newly baptized, he rejoiced greatly, together with all his people.
And the prince, the bishop and the priests called him to them. They blessed him, comforted him, spoke to him words of life, and preached to him the good news of Christ and of eternal life.
And he himself answered them with thanks in words of the true faith, so that they were amazed and glorified God.
And the blessed Abo thanked God all the more, because he saw that land full of faith in Christ, and that no unbeliever was found living within its borders.
For their border is the Pontic Sea, a land inhabited entirely by Christians, reaching as far as the border of Chaldia. Trebizond is there, the settlement of Apsarea, and the harbour of Napsai.
These cities and places are under the rule of the king of the Greeks, a servant of Christ, who has his throne in the great city of Constantinople.
And when the holy and blessed Abo saw the exceeding love of God among the people of that place, and the unceasing prayer of all the people,
he was seized with godly zeal, for he remembered the saying of the holy apostle:
"It is good to be zealous for good at all times." So in those winter days, in the month of January, on the seventeenth of the month,
on the commemoration of the holy father Antony, he too took up that severe labour. In the middle of the city, as if in the desert, he fought against the enemy, the devil.
And through silence and fasting he weakened the flesh of his youth, "so that he might be able to quench all the flaming arrows of the devil."
He remembered our Saviour, how after his holy baptism he went out into the desert
and overcame the crafty tempter, the devil, by prayer and holy fasting for forty days.
In the same way this blessed Abo spoke not a single word among people, but conversed only with God in his holy prayer. In this way he passed three months and persevered in fasting and silence.
And in the holy days of the Great Fast, the seven weeks, only on Sunday and on Saturday, when he received the holy mystery,
the body and blood of Christ, did he then take a little food. So it went until he reached that holy day, the great feast of fulfilment,
the resurrection of Christ our God. Only then did he leave off that severe fast, and he also loosed his tongue from silence and glorified God.
After Nerse's flight from Kartli, Mahdi, the Commander of the Faithful, by the command of God, sent Stephen,
son of Gurgen the eristavi and nephew of Nerse (his sister's son), to be presiding prince of this land of Kartli in place of Nerse, his mother's brother.
Then Nerse was glad, because the Lord had not taken the rule away from his house.
He too became eager, and all the more zealously, and he sent envoys and asked of the rulers,
the amirs of this land, that they would keep him safe from harm, so that he might come out freely with all his people.
And as they were setting out from the land of Abkhazia, the prince of Abkhazia summoned the blessed Abo and said to him:
"Do not leave this land, for the land of Kartli is held by the Saracens, and you are a Saracen by birth. They will not leave you in peace among them as a Christian.
And I fear for you, that they may again turn you aside from the faith of Christ, willingly or unwillingly, and you may lose all your great labour." But the blessed Abo said to him:
"Since Christ has received me, taken away from me the darkness of my former ignorance and made me worthy of his light, I will never deny his name.
even if they give me countless amounts of gold and silver, or judge me with torture and beatings, they will not be able to separate me from the love of my Lord."
"And now do not hold me back, servant of God, for what merit is there in my staying here, where there is neither fear nor death for Christ's sake?
Now I beg you, let me go, so that my Christian faith may be openly made known to those haters of Christ. For I have heard from the holy Gospel what was said by our Saviour:
"No one lights a lamp and puts it under a bushel; instead they put it on a lampstand,
"so that it gives light to all. In the same way, let your light shine before people." So why should I now hide this true light with which Christ has enlightened me?"
I will never hide out of fear of death, for I have learned from the holy Apostle that:
'Nor shall the cowardly [?] inherit the kingdom of God.' For this reason I am not afraid of death, for I seek the kingdom from Christ."
And in this way he persuaded the prince, and the prince let him go.
And he came out with Nerse to the land of Kartli and entered the city of Tbilisi, and he lived there openly as a Christian.
And when the Saracens who were there, who had known him before, saw that he was a Christian, some reproached him,
some insulted him, some threatened him, some persecuted him, and some tried to persuade him with peaceable words.
But he was firmly grounded in Christ and was frightened by no one; for three years he lived openly as a Christian in that city and in all the surrounding villages.
Yet 'no one laid hands on him to do him harm, for his hour had not yet come.'
And the Christ-loving people, who knew of his virtue toward God, provided him with food and clothing.
You who love Christ and love the martyrs, receive from me this blessed account of the holy martyr and champion of Christ, who through his courage and glory was crowned by Christ!

In the reign of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the year eight hundred and forty-six from the Passion and the Resurrection from the dead, when Constantine, son of Leo, reigned in Constantinople, the great city,
over the Christians; when Moses, Amir al-Mu'minin, son of Mahdi, reigned among the Saracens; when Samuel was Catholicos in Kartli,
During the rule of Stephen, son of Gurgen, as prince, when 6,389 years had passed since the beginning, on the sixth of the month of January;
on Friday, the day of the Epiphany, we learned of the martyrdom of this holy and blessed martyr and good contender, Abo, in the city of Tbilisi. It happened in this way.
For a little before these days they had seized this blessed martyr of Christ and brought him before the judge
who was emir in the city of Tbilisi, and they put him in prison for confessing Christ.
But after some days Stephen, the eristavi of Kartli, asked for him to be released, brought him out of prison and let him go.
After a few days the accusers of this holy martyr were stirred up again, angry and raging, full of envy against the Christians.
They plotted together against the saint and went before the judge (for another judge, an emir, had come into the city of Tbilisi), and they said to him:
"In this city there is a young man who was a Saracen by birth, and was raised and lived by the law that Muhammad, our apostle, gave us.
Now he has abandoned this law of ours. He calls himself a Christian, goes about the city without fear, and teaches many of our people to become Christians.
Now order him to be seized, and subject him to torture and beating until he confesses the law of Muhammad, our apostle.
If he does not, put him to death, so that many do not come to imitate him because of his words."
While they were making this accusation, some Christian men heard of it. They went quickly and told the blessed Abo:
"Look, they are seeking you now in order to seize you, torture you and beat you." And they urged him to flee and hide. But he said to them:
"I am prepared not only for torture for Christ's sake, but also for death." And he went out joyfully and moved about openly in the streets.
Then the judge's servants came, seized the blessed Abo and brought him before the judge.
The judge said to him, "What is this I hear about you? You are a Saracen by race and tribe, yet you have abandoned the law of your fathers and gone astray with the Christians?

Now make yourself ready and pray according to the law in which your parents raised you." But the blessed Abo was strengthened by Christ, was filled with the spirit of faith, and said to the judge, the emir:
"You have said this rightly. I am a Saracen by nature, born into it on my father's side and my mother's side.
I was taught the law of Muhammad and lived by it while I was in ignorance. But when it pleased God,
who chose me from among my brothers and kinsmen and saved me through Jesus Christ, his Son and my God,
and made me understand the better good, then I abandoned that former law, composed by human skill, and that belief contrived by the cleverness of fables.
Now I have followed the true faith, granted through Christ, in the Holy Trinity, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
In this faith I have been baptized, and this I also worship, for this is the true God. And now I am a Christian beyond all dispute."
The judge said to him: "Give up this mad intention. If you have followed the Christians because you are in need, I will give you even greater gifts and honour right now."
The blessed Abo said to him: "Keep your gold and your silver for yourself, for your own destruction. I do not seek honour from men,
for I have a gift from Christ: the crown of life and incorruption, and eternal honour in the heavens."
Then the judge ordered that he be bound hand and foot with iron fetters, and so they threw him into prison.
But the blessed one rejoiced, gave thanks to the Lord and said:
"I thank you, O Lord and Saviour, our God, Jesus Christ, for you have made me worthy of judgement and imprisonment for the sake of your holy name."
This took place on the twenty-seventh of the month of December, on a Tuesday, on the commemoration of the apostle of Christ,
the first deacon and first martyr and commander of all the martyrs, Saint Stephen.
It was right and fitting that the commander of all the martyrs should exert himself on his behalf, together with all the martyrs like him,
so that this last martyr of Christ too might not be kept from being counted alongside them in their courage.
The blessed Abo stayed in the prison, fasting, praying and singing psalms night and day without rest, and he did works of charity,
for he sold everything he had and fed the hungry and needy who were imprisoned with him.
But the false teachers and the accusers would go in to him, and some of them spoke to him with flattering words, as it were:
"Son, do not throw yourself away. Do not trade away your youth by being a Christian, and do not cut yourself off from your brothers and your kin,
so that you do not bring harm on yourself and grieve all of us." And some of them tried to frighten him, saying to him:
"What good will that Christ of yours do you? Or who will deliver you from our hands? For fire and torments have already been prepared for you, unless you come back to us."
But the blessed man did not listen to them. Instead he prayed and sang psalms without ceasing in his mind. After they had talked at length, he said to them:
"Do not say anything to me, for I was like a deaf man who did not hear, and like a mute who does not open his mouth.
I became like a man who does not hear, in whose mouth there is no word, for I hope in the Lord.
"Depart from me, you evildoers, and I will search out the commandments of my God." When they could not move that righteous man, they went away from there in shame.
The blessed one was in prison for nine days. Every day he fasted, and he kept vigil through the night until dawn.
On the ninth day he said to all the Christians imprisoned with him, and to the others as well:
"Tomorrow is my departure from the flesh and my going to my Lord and God Jesus Christ." For the Lord had revealed this to his martyr.

Then he took off his clothes and gave them to be sold, so that with the money they might buy him wax candles for lighting and incense. He sent these to all the churches of the city so that they would light them.
He also sent word to all the priests, begging them to pray for him, so that he might not stumble from faith in Christ and might be made worthy of the contest of Christ's martyrs.
On the night of the holy feast, at the vigil, he took two large candles in his hands and stood in the middle of the prison.
He remained standing on his feet until dawn without sitting down at all, until he had finished the psalms and the candles had burned out in his hands.
His hands were fastened with iron to his neck. Standing there without moving, he said:
"I saw the Lord always before me, for he is at my right hand, so that I may not be moved," and the words that follow.
And when that tenth day dawned, the feast of the Baptism of the Savior, which falls on the sixth of the month of January, that day was a Friday.
And the blessed one said: "This day is great for me, for I see the twofold victory of my Lord Jesus Christ.
For on this feast he went down, stripped, into the river Jordan to be baptized, and in the depth of the waters he crushed the heads of the hidden dragon by the power of his Godhead.
It is fitting for me too on this day to strip off the fear of this flesh of mine, which is the garment of my soul, and to go down, as into the depth of the sea,
in the middle of this city, and to be baptized with my blood and with fire and the Spirit, as John the Forerunner preached; and then to go down again into the waters too, and to be illumined again.
For today is the descent of the Holy Spirit upon all waters, by which those who believe in Christ are baptized, in the likeness of the streams of the Jordan.
And by stripping off my flesh I will bring to nothing the schemes that the crafty enemy devised against me, and I will trample them under my foot in the middle of this city.

And again, on this day, Friday, my Lord Jesus Christ, through his passion and by stretching out his hands on the cross, exposed the enemy of the whole world and made him something to be pointed at by all the ends of the earth.
Now it is fitting for me too to go out to fight against that enemy of the Christians and, by shedding my blood for Christ, to make him a laughingstock and an object of scorn" to all Christians.
"For he thought that by the fear of death he could separate me from the love of my Lord Jesus Christ.
But I will make his plan a disgrace and defeat him with help from Christ, and I will pay back both of the debts I owe my Lord."
Then he asked for water, washed his face, anointed his head with oil, and said:
"Once I was a perfumer myself, skilled at preparing fragrant ointments, but this ointment is for the day of my burial.
From now on I will no longer anoint myself with this perishable oil of my earthly exile, but, as the wise Solomon taught me in the Song of Songs:
'I ran after the fragrance of your ointments,' O Christ, who have filled me with the imperishable fragrance of faith and of love for you.
You know, O Lord, that I have loved you more than myself!"
When he had said this, he sent to the holy church, and they brought him the holy mystery, the Body and Blood of Christ.
It was the third hour of that great feast day. When he had received that true and life-giving mystery, he said:
"I thank you, my Lord and God, Jesus Christ, who have given me your body, which grants life, as provision for my journey, and your precious blood for my joy and strength!
Now I know that you will not abandon me, but you abide with me and I with you.
From now on I will no longer receive any other food, from which I would be hungry again, nor any other drink, from which I would be thirsty again; this is enough for my eternal life.
Now, 'even though I walk among the shadows of death, I will fear no evil, for you, Lord, are with me.'"
As soon as he had said this, the judge's servants arrived. He parted from all the Christians who were imprisoned and said to them:
"Remember me in your prayers, for you will not see me again in this passing world!" They led him out just as he was, in fetters on his feet and hands.
He was led through the middle of the city, and the Christians and his acquaintances who saw him wept for him. But Saint Abo said to them:
"Do not weep over me, but rejoice, for I am going to my Lord. Send me on my way with prayer, and may the peace of the Lord keep you!"
As he went along, he regarded his own body the way someone who escorts a dead man regards the dead.
And having become a traveller in his spirit, he himself recited the 118th Psalm:
"Blessed are those who are blameless in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord." Afterwards, as the hymn of kneeling, he said the words of the blessed thief:
"Remember me, O Lord, when you come in your kingdom."
In this way he reached the gate of the judge, the emir. When he arrived, he boldly made the sign of the cross on the gate and also signed himself with the cross.
They brought him before the judge, and the judge said to him: "What is it, young man? What have you decided for yourself?"
The holy martyr was filled with the Holy Spirit and said to him: "I have decided, and I am a Christian!"
The judge said to him, "Have you not given up your madness and foolishness?" The blessed Abo said to him:
"If I had remained in ignorance and folly, I would not have been made worthy to follow Christ!"
The judge said to him: "Do you not realize that these words of yours will bring death upon you?"
Saint Abo said to him: "If I die, I believe that I will live with Christ. But why are you dragging this out?
"Whatever you intend for me, do it, for, like that wall against which you are leaning,
so I do not hear those vain words of yours, for my mind is with Christ in heaven!" The judge said to him:
"What such great sweetness do you have from your Christ, that you do not pity yourself even unto death?" Saint Abo said to him:
"If you wish to know his sweetness, you too believe in Christ and be baptized into him, and only then will you be made worthy to know his sweetness."
Then the emir became angry and ordered that he be taken outside and his head be cut off.
The servants brought him out beyond the gates, into the courtyard of the palace, and they released his hands and feet from the iron bonds.
The blessed one quickly tore off the clothes he was wearing by himself, and, stripped bare, he sealed his face and body with the sign of the cross and said:
"I thank you and bless you, O Holy Trinity, for you have made me worthy to share in the struggle of your holy martyrs!"
When he had said this, he put his hands behind him on his back in the form of a cross. With a joyful face and a bold spirit he cried out to Christ, and he bowed his neck to the sword.
They struck him with the sword three times, because they thought that fear of death would make him turn away from Christ.
But the holy martyr took the sword bravely and in silence, until he gave up his soul to the Lord.
When the enemies of Christ, the accusers of the holy martyr, saw this,
that the blessed one had been made perfect in Christ, had fought the good fight, and had overcome their fury by faith and endurance,
they were filled with even more envy. They went in before the ruler and said to him: "We know that the Christians have this custom:

if anyone gets himself killed for the sake of their Christ, they steal his body and honour it with burial. Then they lie and spread stories among the people of signs and healings, as if he had worked them.
They divide up his clothing, the hair of his head and his bones, supposedly as [?] for the sick. In this way they lure in many ignorant people.
So now, order his body to be given to us, so that we may take it away, burn it with fire, destroy it completely, and wipe out this delusion of the Christians,
so that everyone may see it and be afraid. Then some of them may turn to us, and our own people will be afraid and will no longer follow the teaching of the Christians."
Although they said this out of envy toward the Christians, they were still bearing witness to what is true and right,
since the martyrs of Christ are indeed healers and intercessors for all who come to them with love and faith in Christ.
The judge said to them: "Take him wherever you want, and do as you see fit!"
Then they went out and lifted his honoured body from the ground. They put it, together with his clothing, into a basket for carrying.
They also dug the spilled blood of the righteous one out of the ground, leaving nothing at all of it in the earth, and they put that into a vessel too.
They placed the saint on a cart, in the same way as those brave Holy Forty. For the place where they had cut off the holy martyr's head
was at the doors of the holy church that had been founded in the name of the Holy Forty. So it was fitting that he should be like those valiant Holy Forty Martyrs.
They carried the holy body of the saint out of the city and took it up to the place called the Place of Lamentation, because the graves of the people of that city are there.
There they took it down from the cart and laid it on the ground. They brought firewood, hay and naphtha, poured them over the holy body, and set it on fire.
They kept it burning until they had burned up the flesh of the holy martyr. This happened at a place east of the city's citadel, which is called Sadilego,
on the face of the rock, which is a cliff: the rocky bank of the great river that flows past the city on the east. That river is called the Mtkvari (Kura).
They did not allow any of the Christians to go to that place until they had finished burning the flesh of the holy martyr. But as for the bones of the holy martyr,
They gathered the remains they could no longer burn into a sheepskin, tied them up tightly, took them away and threw them into the great river,
under the city bridge, where the venerable cross of the bridge had been set up.
So the water of that river became a garment wrapped around those holy bones, and the depth of the waters became the tomb of that holy martyr, so that no one might approach them carelessly.
This is what the enemies of Christ did, and this is how the blessed one fought the good fight.
Then the Christian multitude of the city began to throw off their fear of the tyrants, and they all went out to the place
where the body of the holy martyr had been burned. The old men came running with their staffs, the lame leaped like deer, and the young men ran;
the children came scrambling over one another. The women were like the holy myrrh-bearers, who ran carrying spices to the holy tomb of Christ our God.
These women were truly like them, for they ran in tears, carrying candles and incense in their hands.
They all went with joy and with thanks to Christ, and they even took up the earth of that place. Many brought people who were gripped by illnesses, and these were healed on that very day.
But Almighty God showed his power even more. He honoured his martyr and showed a wonderful sign, so that all would know that he is a disciple of Christ.
As the day turned to evening, at the first hour of the night, the Lord sent down a shining star over that place,
like a lamp of fire. It stood for a long time over the place where the blessed martyr of Christ had been burned.
It stood up in the air for about three hours of that night, or more. It gave off a brightness that was not like the fire of this earth but like the terrifying power of lightning.
All the citizens saw it: the judge too, and all the people, the Christian inhabitants, all the Saracens, and the strangers who had come from elsewhere.
For a long time they watched it with their own eyes, until it even troubled the tyrants. Some of the servants of the judge, the emir, went to look at the place,
for they thought the Christians might have lit a candle there. As they drew near the place, they saw
that the star rose up into the air. They could not approach the place, because they were seized by a fear sent from God.
And again on the second night the waters gave forth an even more marvellous light;
those to whom that heavenly fire, upon the earth and beneath the air, had seemed [?], wanted to conceal those wonders,
but again the waters could not hold it back, and the fierce, surging waves and depths could not put it out.
Under the bridge, where they had thrown the God-honoured bones of the blessed martyr, lights shone out like a pillar,
like lightning, and again they stood for a long time. All around the banks of the river, the rock, the cliffs and the bridge were lit up
from top to bottom. The whole multitude of the city saw this as well, so that all would believe that truly Jesus Christ
…of the Son of God, it is clear. Let all who believe in Christ and all who do not understand that the word of the Lord is true,
which he spoke: "If anyone serves me, my Father who is in heaven will honor him."
If he has already shown such great honor to that corruptible body even now,
how much more, at the incorruptible resurrection of the righteous, will they see him crowned with glory and honor among the angels, and be ashamed of their foolish madness,
those who denied Christ and beat, persecuted and slew his saints, while the Lord received them into heaven!
And now, beloved, from now on it is right for us all the more to accept those former blessed martyrs as well,
so that, because of this new martyr whom we have seen, we may believe in the former ones too, and say the words of blessed David:
"Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints." For to him belongs glory, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen!
Now come, you believers in Christ, and let us celebrate the commemoration of this new holy martyr,
whom Christ has granted to all this land of ours, Kartli, as an intercessor for us. With great joy let us open the treasuries
of our hearts and minds, and with cheerful faces and clear tongues let us praise his good struggle and say:
"Rejoice, blessed martyr of the Lord!
For you, the last laborer of our Savior, hired at the eleventh hour, caught up with the day-laborers who rose at dawn, and you did not fall short of their wage!
"Rejoice, martyr of the Lord!
For you became like Paul, the last of the apostles, by casting off your ancestral laws and teachings and by confessing Christ the Son of God, and like him you had your head cut off.
"Now who could praise you worthily, you who are truly worthy of praise?
I wish to praise you, all-praised martyr of Christ, but I do not dare, for the praise of your virtues has risen higher than my mind can reach.
Yet I am also afraid to keep silent, for you loved me with that blessed love that comes from Christ while you were still in this world of ours.
May it not happen that, because my tongue holds back from praising you, the work of your intercession for me before Christ is also held back!
So, receiving the grace of Christ through you, I will praise you as far as I am able, you who are adorned with beauty by the Lord!
"Rejoice, rejoice, blessed martyr of the Lord!
For without having seen, by faith and by courageous confession, you gained the blessedness of the holy apostles of Christ, who saw with their eyes and served with their hands.
"For the heavenly Father crowned you through his only-begotten Son and filled you with the grace of the Holy Spirit!
"The Son received you from the Father, and the Holy Spirit glorified you!
"The Holy Spirit loved you and, in his unity with the Father and the Son, honored you and revealed you as victor in the contest!
"The order of angels marvelled at you, for, as one without a body, you endured death for Christ's sake.
"The patriarchs rejoice over you, for blessed Abraham received you, one of his offspring, into his bosom for the sake of Christ,
whom he received in his own tent, and through whom he was shown to be the father of many nations.
"You became the fruit of the martyrs of Christ and a disciple of the apostles!
"Among the martyrs your name was written in the register of the heavenly King, and you were crowned together with the martyrs!
"You were given your place among the confessors, and you are glorified together with the righteous!
"We marvel greatly at you, holy martyr. In this very time, the reign of the Ishmaelites, you willingly chose lowliness over glory
for Christ's sake. You cast away that law upheld by the sword, confessed the true one, and worshipped the Crucified One as Lord and God!
"Where, or from whom, did you learn such knowledge of Christ? What wonder raised you up to the glory of the Kingdom?
"Truly you resembled the thief on the right hand. For you too had, among those held prisoner with you, one who was born of Christians,
who had turned away from Christ and followed a foreign law. He was again being judged with you for confessing Christ, but that wretched man stumbled once more and fell.
For out of fear of death he loved this passing world and lost the eternal one. The evil enemy snatched him away, and that sheep of Christ was torn by the beast.
For he separated himself from the good Shepherd and threw away from his hands the staff of Christ's power. For this reason he was overcome and was driven out of the flock of rational sheep.
But you, blessed martyr, Christ guarded with that rod, his cross, in keeping with your strong faith in him.
"You equalled that thief in faith and were given your place in Paradise!
"You opened the gate of Paradise by the cross of Christ, and the fiery cherubim who guard it did not question you about who you are!
And what more shall I say? For "the Lord suffered for us, the innocent for the guilty," and shed his own spotless blood.
And you repaid the debt, for you too shed your own blood out of love for him.
Therefore he adorned you with the crown of victory and made you an heir of his Father's Kingdom.
"Through you, holy martyr, Christ's love for us and our faith in him have been renewed. For we had mingled with a foreign people,
apostate from Christ by their law, a race that loves this passing world, a seed that does not believe in the Son of God, revilers of our faith.
From them we learned their deeds, and by imitating them we served the desires of our hearts, like people without hope in Christ who had forgotten eternal life.
But now through you Christ has drawn near to us. We have again come to understand the fear of him and his love, and we have been made worthy of his grace,
and of his love and mercy, through the many miracles and healings he shows among us day after day!
"Your foolish sacrificers, by sword and fire, made you shine brighter than flame. Those senseless men did not understand the word of the Lord,
that "the time will come when everyone who kills you will think that he has offered a sacrifice to God."
O their folly, and more than folly! For no one knew you before: who you were, of what family, of what people,
or by what law you lived. But now, against their will, they have made you known as a confessor of Christ and shown you to everyone as a martyr.
"All created things have honoured you, for heaven is a witness
to your righteousness. It sent down a wondrous fire upon the place where you were offered up like a spotless lamb, roasted by fire.
The earth offered you up to God as a holy and pleasing sacrifice through the burning of your honourable body, for it became for you
like the altars of Abel, Enoch, Abraham and Elijah, who offered lambs to God as whole burnt offerings.
And again, the place of your sacrifice was like the censer of the priests Aaron and Zechariah. For upon the burning coals there rose up
the fragrance of your flesh like the sweet smell of incense, before the Lord, into the Holy of Holies, the heavenly altar!
"The rivers received you as a martyr of Christ, and Christ God lit up the darkness of their depths with heavenly light.
"Your kinsmen made you a stranger and an outcast. But Christ chose you out from among the Ishmaelites, like a rose from among thorns, and offered you to his own Church!
"Christ took you, a wild olive tree, and planted you in the garden of his own inheritance to bear the fruit of blessing.
With the fruit of your faith he gladdened the Church. In it the believers in Christ rejoice and call blessed your glory,
your struggle, your courage, your martyrdom, your crown!
"How can I praise you, holy martyr, victor in the contest?
For you, a new believer in Christ, became a teacher to us. You gave the learned more understanding, you made the wavering firmer, you made the steadfast joyful,
and you made the pagans eager to serve Christ. You left us the memory of your martyrdom, and we have become heralds who tell your name to everyone!
"Now we all appeal to your love for Christ. Be an intercessor before the Saviour of all for all of us who, through you, ask mercy from Christ God,
to whom belong glory, honour and power, together with the Father and the all-holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen!
